summary: Post-v0.3 release-hardening and release-scope-reassessment phase (bounded; not an architecture-expansion phase). Reconstructed the complete post-v0.3 change inventory directly from git diff v0.3.0..HEAD: 31 commits, 6 production files, +350/-107 lines, every change traceable to 2W/2W.1 (generic producer intake helper) or 2X/2X.1 (codex-ox registration), zero unrelated/deferred changes. Derived a release-candidate capability set, a stable-vs-current-vs-proposed capability matrix, and a full supported-agent matrix directly from live source inspection (MULTI_AGENT_REGISTRY, AGENT_CONFIG_REGISTRY, _LOCKABLE_BACKENDS, _build_invoke_command, build_remote_policy), reconfirming that 'registered agent' is never confused with 'PCAE-native executable backend' for any of the nine registered identities. Adjudicated both carried-forward W.1 findings: independently reproduced the malformed-agent-lock defect fresh, traced its exact mechanism (a packaged CLI command, pcae intake from-files, crashed with a raw uncaught traceback on a corrupted lock file; pcae session bootstrap was accidentally unaffected because json.JSONDecodeError happens to subclass ValueError), reclassified it SHOULD-FIX-BEFORE-RELEASE, and repaired it this phase with narrowly-scoped bounded hardening in derive_producer_provenance (fails closed with a clean malformed_agent_lock: rejection reason, does not silently fall through to the no-lock path, does not touch the lower-level read_agent_lock function's own contract). Reconfirmed the empty-agent_id finding as SAFE-TO-DEFER (cannot impersonate a registered identity; producer identity has zero authority effect either way) and deliberately left it unrepaired per this phase's own instruction against introducing registry-membership requirements. Found README.md and docs/QUICKSTART_V0_3.md were stale -- neither mentioned the packaged pcae intake from-files command or codex-ox at all -- and repaired both additively, without altering any v0.3.0-labeled historical claim. Verified the package boundary by building real local wheel and sdist candidate artifacts in a disposable venv (python -m build) and confirming both include every production file this release line touches; ran a clean-environment install smoke against both artifacts covering session bootstrap, pcae intake from-files, intake show/list, no-lock direct intake with an arbitrary producer, and codex-ox bootstrap/provenance end-to-end, with zero external network or AI-service calls at any point. Recommends v0.3.1 (patch) with documented semantic-version rationale: every change is additive identity registration, consolidation of the existing v0.3.0 generic-intake feature, or small bounded hardening, with no breaking change to any existing CLI surface, JSON schema, or authority semantic. Produced a release-blocker table with zero remaining BLOCKING or MUST-FIX items scoped to this phase's own production changes; the one MUST-FIX item found (pyproject.toml's stale 0.3.0 version string) is explicitly a publish-time action correctly deferred to the next phase, not a code defect. 9 fresh independent tests plus 439 targeted regression plus test_agent.py+test_session.py full files (4381 passed, 0 failed) = 4829 tests run and passing this phase. Independent Fast Green A/B (fixed git worktree clean baseline vs. this phase's working tree) shows zero attributable regressions: the raw 18-failure delta is 16 unrelated historical dirty-src/pcae-tree guard tests (resolves on commit) plus 2 independently-confirmed concurrent-load subprocess-timeout artifacts, with one flip consistent with the same load sensitivity. Assessed article readiness as READY AFTER RELEASE with an explicit scoping caveat (the truthful integration story is generic adapter-free intake plus codex-ox as an example, not a claim that DeepSeek/Gemini/Grok/Perplexity are supported integrations -- those four remain pre-v0.3.0 undeclared-adapter placeholders) -- the article file itself was not read, modified, or published. Zero Blocking findings.
